result.topic_en: The page gives a general formula for figurate numbers with a parameter a, then two Diophantine fragments: a multiplier that rationalizes a quadratic expression in x when x^3=m, and solutions of xy(xx−yy)=a n^2 for the primes a=7 and a=13.

(Krafft.)

Omnes illae superiores series numerorum figuratorum sequenti forma generali comprehendi possunt
$1;\ \frac{n+a}{1};\ \frac{(n+1)(n+2a)}{1.2};\ \frac{(n+1)(n+2)(n+3a)}{1.2.3};\ \frac{(n+1)(n+2)(n+3)(n+4a)}{1.2.3.4}$ etc.
pro qua superior littera $T$ fit $=a+2n-2$.
A. m. T. I. p. 234. 235.

C. Analysis Diophantea.

a) Quaestiones ad resolutionem unius aequationis ducentes.

37.
(J. A. Euler.)

Problema. Si fuerit $x^3=m$, et proposita sit formula $axx+bx+c$, invenire multiplicatorem $pxx+qx+r$, ut productum $(axx+bx+c)(pxx+qx+r)$
fiat numerus absolutus non amplius involvens $x$, posito scilicet $x^3=m$.
Solutio. Productum ergo erit
$mapx+(aq+bp)m+(ar+bq+cp)xx$
$+(br+cq)x+cr.$
Debet ergo poni $br+cq+map=0$ et $ar+bq+cp=0$, tum enim productum erit
$m(aq+bp)+cr.$
Fit autem $p=\frac{-br-cq}{ma}=\frac{-ar-bq}{c}$,
unde fit $bcr+ccq=maar+mabq$; hinc $mabq-ccq=bcr-maar$,
consequenter $\frac{q}{r}=\frac{bc-maa}{mab-cc}$.
Capiatur ergo $q=bc-maa$, $r=mab-cc$, erit $p=ac-bb$; ita ut multiplicator quaesitus sit
$(ac-bb)xx+(bc-maa)x+mab-cc$;
ac tum productum erit $3mabc-m^2a^3-mb^3-c^3$.
A. m. T. I. p. 50. 51.

38.

Problema. Invenire numeros $x$ et $y$, ut fiat $xy(xx-yy)=ann$, existente $a$ numero primo: ubi hi casus sunt notandi:
I. Si $a=7$, sumatur $x=16$ et $y=9$, tum enim fit $xy(xx-yy)=7.16.9.25$.
II. Si $a=13$, sumatur $x=325$ et $y=36$, erit $xy(xx-yy)=13.25.36.361.289$.

methods.what: General term formula for the generalized figurate number series with parameter a, with T = a+2n−2
Rationalizing multiplier for a quadratic in a cube root (norm form): with x^3=m, (axx+bx+c) times this multiplier is free of x
Resulting product (the norm) as an absolute number
Method: set the coefficients of x and xx to zero and solve the resulting linear conditions for p, q, r
Particular solutions of xy(x^2−y^2)=a n^2 for a=7 and a=13

items.english: If x^3=m and the formula axx+bx+c is proposed, find a multiplier pxx+qx+r such that the product (axx+bx+c)(pxx+qx+r) becomes an absolute number no longer involving x, given of course that x^3=m.
